executive_branch.role: Resigned Sept 2021 after millions in trades during Fed COVID interventions
Omitted fund switches during blackout; term ended Jan 2022
Family trust bond trades disclosed during 2020 blackout

notable_cases.details: Sold stock after private Senate briefings before COVID market crash. Chaired Senate Intelligence Committee.
notable_cases.outcome: DOJ investigation closed 2021 with no charges. SEC settled 2024.

notable_cases.details: Sold stock and bought Citrix (remote-work stock) after Senate coronavirus briefing.
Extensive trading around COVID briefings including Cardlytics and Pfizer.
Husband sold Allogene stock after COVID briefings.
notable_cases.outcome: Investigation closed. Feinstein said she was not involved in trades.

notable_cases.details: Sold stock in late January after COVID briefings.
Made 327 stock purchases on April 8, 2025, the day before pausing tariffs — market rallied ~9% on tariff pause news.
notable_cases.outcome: No formal investigation. Widely reported by NBC News, Bloomberg.

notable_cases.details: First president disclosing this scale of active trading. 82% of transactions late-filed (STOCK Act violation range).
notable_cases.outcome: Paid $200 STOCK Act late fees on at least 2 filings.

notable_cases.details: Traded during Fed COVID-19 emergency interventions. Held positions >$1M in tech and energy names.
Traded REITs and other assets while Fed intervened in mortgage/credit markets.
Amended disclosures to include previously omitted trades during 2020 market intervention period.
notable_cases.outcome: Term ended Jan 2022. No formal action.

notable_cases.details: Repeated violations of Fed blackout window trading rules over 5-year period.
Husband bought $1M–$5M NVDA call options weeks before major moves. Reported 70.9% return in 2024.
Highest-volume individual-stock trader in Senate. Serves on Armed Services Committee.
Highest all-time volume in Congress; chairs Foreign Affairs. Trades primarily through diversified holdings.

notable_cases.case: Sources: ProPublica, NBC News, Bloomberg, Wikipedia (2020 congressional insider trading scandal), Business Insider, Inman, Democracy Defenders Fund, Unusual Whales. Full URLs in Sources sheet.
